subject: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily@brightops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration

Emily —

Great talking yesterday. Following up with a written summary of the partner commercial mechanics we propose for BrightOps' integration into the Redwood Marketplace and resale channels. High level: we want to make sure originators get credit quickly, while protecting booking accuracy and limiting retro exposure.

Proposed commercial terms (draft):
- Originator credit: 10% of net ARR on first-year bookings introduced by BrightOps, 7% thereafter for renewals attributable to the original opportunity.
- Originator claim window: 180 days from first qualified intro for primary credit; claims after 180 days considered on a case-by-case basis with supporting evidence.
- Lead registration: registrant must submit a HubSpot registration and have a qualifying discovery call within 14 days; registration portal will be the canonical record.
- Retroactive rebates: eligible if Redwood books business where BrightOps was the documented originator but paperwork completes after the quarter close; rebate calculation is limited to a 12-month lookback and capped at 15% of the quarter's gross bookings to limit operational risk.
- Disputes: first-touch wins by default; overlap resolution uses objective timestamped evidence (HubSpot registration, calendar invite, MPV).

Operational notes:
- We publish a partner dashboard for registrations and claim status; quarterly settlement runs within 30 days of quarter close.
- Attachment: redwood-partner-appendix.pdf (commercial appendix + definitions) and mutual-action-plan.xlsx to align milestones.

Ask: can you confirm BrightOps is comfortable with a 180-day originator window and the 15% retro cap? If yes, we can route a short MOU and DocuSign for signature. If you prefer a shorter claim window (e.g., 90 days) or a different cap, call that out and we can escalate to Channel Finance.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Carter <emily@brightops.com>

Subject: Re: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful and clear. A few follow-ups from procurement and our GTM team: 

1) Lead registration window: 14 days is fine, but can we get confirmation on what constitutes a "qualifying discovery call"? Is a calendar invite and attendance by at least one BrightOps AE enough, or do you require meeting notes in HubSpot?

2) The 180-day claim window is longer than we typically see in our reseller agreements. We usually push for 120 days. Would Redwood consider 120 days for public leads and 180 days for enterprise (contact-based) introductions?

3) Retro cap: the 15% cap seems reasonable, but we need clarity on how refunds/cancellations are netted. Also, is the cap applied per-quarter or per-year?

4) Please share the mutual action plan; our legal wants to see the sample MOU language before committing to DocuSign.

Can you loop in whoever owns settlement and carve-outs? I'll also include our procurement alias (procurement@brightops.com) for contract velocity.

Best,
Emily Carter
Head of Alliances
BrightOps
emily@brightops.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration

Emily —

Thanks for the quick notes. Answers inline and next steps below.

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 11:03 AM Emily Carter <emily@brightops.com> wrote:
> 1) Lead registration window: 14 days is fine, but can we get confirmation on what constitutes a "qualifying discovery call"?

A qualifying discovery call = a calendar event with >=1 BrightOps AE and >=1 Redwood AE (or PM) plus a short HubSpot activity note that confirms the customer problem and next-step (e.g., evaluation, pricing call, or technical POC). We use the HubSpot note and invite timestamp as evidence for registration disputes. If you prefer, we can accept a signed NDA or SOW in lieu of the HubSpot note for enterprise deals.

> 2) The 180-day claim window is longer than we typically see in our reseller agreements. We usually push for 120 days. Would Redwood consider 120 days for public leads and 180 days for enterprise (contact-based) introductions?

We can do a tiered window: 120 days for inbound/public marketing-sourced leads, 180 days for named-account/contact-based introductions where BrightOps provides a list and outreach history. We'll add language to the appendix.

> 3) Retro cap: the 15% cap seems reasonable, but we need clarity on how refunds/cancellations are netted. Also, is the cap applied per-quarter or per-year?

Cap is applied per-quarter to simplify settlement. Refunds and chargebacks will be netted from the gross bookings before rebate calculation; in exceptional cases (true-ups), we'll run an adjustment in the following quarter.

> 4) Please share the mutual action plan; our legal wants to see the sample MOU language before committing to DocuSign.

Attached: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline + milestones). I've asked Legal to provide a short one-page MOU that captures the commercial bullets above. Ben, can you take the MOU redline and flag any mandatory legal exceptions we should surface early?

Next steps / action items:
- Ben (Legal) to provide MOU redline and call out carve-outs (3 business days).
- Marissa (Channel Rev) to confirm settlement cadence and payout schedule for a first-year funnel (we'll share sample calc).
- Emily / BrightOps to confirm acceptance of tiered claim window and full MOU once Ben's redline is in.

I'll prep a short DocuSign once we have the final MOU language.

Thanks —
Hannah
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration

Folks —

Quick legal note and a few proposed clarifications for the MOU: 
- Definitions: ensure "originator" is defined as the party with the first documented HubSpot registration or signed statement of introduction; include language for joint-sourced opportunities (split per agreed formula).
- Exceptions: we need a carve-out for opportunities where a prior NDA/SOW exists with Redwood that pre-dates the registration; those are excluded from new originator claims.
- Retro timing: the 12-month lookback should be limited to bookings that can be directly traced to BrightOps activity; we'll require supporting evidence for each retro claim.
- Audit rights: Redwood reserves audit rights on partner-submitted evidence with 30 days advance notice; typical security and data handling clauses will apply.

I attached partner-exception-request-form.pdf as the template BrightOps would use to request an exception to standard claims policy. If BrightOps needs a special carve-out (e.g., named-account list with historical outreach), complete the form and we'll fast-track review.

I'll drop a redline of the MOU in DocuSign and share via the HubSpot link Hannah referenced. Expect a first-draft redline today EOD.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Carter <emily@brightops.com>

Subject: Re: Channel originator claim window and retro rebates - BrightOps integration

Thanks all — we reviewed and BrightOps accepts the tiered claim window (120/180) and the quarterly 15% retro cap with refunds netted before calculation. We'll fill out the exception form for our named-account backbook (we have a list of 38 accounts).

Next step: Hannah / Marissa, please send the MOU redline and a short DocuSign for signature. Also, could we lock a 30-minute sync to review the mutual action plan and handoffs? I'm available Thu 10–12 PT.

Grateful for the quick turnaround — excited to get BrightOps into the Marketplace.

Best,
Emily
